title: Open coefficient tensor respects evaluation and finite Tor bounds
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi$, and $1\le m\le n$. Set $A=\mathcal O_E/(\varpi^n)$, $B=\mathcal O_E/(\varpi^m)$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. For a separated finite-type $k$-scheme $Y$ [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], write $a_Y:Y\to s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $F_{Y,R}=Ra_{Y,R!}\dashv G_{Y,R}=a_{Y,R}^{\times}$, $\omega_{Y,R}=G_{Y,R}R_s$, and $\varepsilon_{Y,R}:F_{Y,R}\omega_{Y,R}\to R_s$, for $R=A,B$, on ordinary small etale module derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-amb-etale-compact-support, thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint]. Let $T_Y=-\otimes_A^LB$ [def-kun-derived-tensor], and denote the canonical compact-support coefficient comparison by $c_{Y,K}:T_sF_{Y,A}K\to F_{Y,B}T_YK$ [lem-fix-compact-support-coefficient-change]. Here bounded constructible finite-Tor means constructible cohomology, zero outside a finite interval, and integers $a\le b$ such that tensoring with every degree-zero module sheaf has cohomology only in $[a,b]$ [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes, def-kun-tor-amplitude]. Let $j:U\hookrightarrow Y$ be a quasi-compact open immersion with $Y$ Noetherian, and let $W\in D^b_{ctf}(Y_{\mathrm{et}},A)$. Put $L=j^*W$, let $e_{R,V}:j_{!,R}j^*V\to V$ be evaluation, and use the coefficient/pullback identification $j^*T_YW\cong T_UL$ [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero, prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact, lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. The canonical $B$-linear open tensor comparison is an isomorphism $d_L:T_Yj_{!,A}L\cong j_{!,B}T_UL$ [lem-pur-etale-open-derived-tensor]. It satisfies
$$e_{B,T_YW}\circ d_L=T_Y(e_{A,W}).$$
Both $j_{!,A}L$ and $j_{!,B}T_UL$ are bounded constructible finite-Tor, and if $L$ has Tor amplitude $[a,b]$ then these two objects have Tor amplitude $[a,b]$ over $A$ and $B$, respectively. Their cohomology stratifications are obtained by extension of a finite locally closed constructibility stratification on $U$, adding the closed complement with zero cohomology. The evaluation identity holds for the canonical direct-sum total tensor comparison on K-flat tensor representatives before derived localization, so it is an equality of derived morphisms, rather than an inference from equality of arbitrary derived maps on stalks.

proof.text: Use the actual ordinary and derived adjunctions of def-sf-etale-open-scalar-data. The inverse of the unique-left-adjoint comparison is the iterated inverse mate. Apply mateEquiv_counit_symm and cancel the comparison isomorphism to obtain the derived evaluation equality. For ordinary evaluation, identify the scalar/restriction mate with openScalarRestrictionZero using the ordinary_reverse_eq and openRestrictScalarsIso_inv_eq calculations already proved in the imported modules. The same mate-counit calculation gives equality of ordinary natural transformations. Apply mapHomologicalComplex and evaluate at P; this proves the before-localization assertion for every complex, hence for the stated K-flat representatives.

Translate finite-value bounded constructibility to the source boundedConstructible predicate via lem-weil-pbc-constructible-etale-module-sheaf-comparison. Exact inverse image preserves bounded constructibility and gives L=j^*W. For either exact restriction or extension by zero, choose the bounded flat representative from exists_iso_Q_obj_flat_of_torAmplitudeIn. Apply the exact functor degreewise, using preservation of flat objects, then torAmplitudeIn_Q_obj_of_flat and mapDerivedCategoryFactors to transport the same Tor interval. This uses the existing source flat-model API, not a new resolution or choice of scalar comparison. Source boundedConstructible_mapDerivedCategory_openImmersionLowerShriek similarly supplies bounded constructibility after extension.

On the Noetherian quasi-compact open U apply exists_etaleScalarFlatModel to L and any given interval [a,b]. Its last two clauses give constructible cohomology and the same B-Tor interval for scalarExtension(phi,U)(L). Tor amplitude implies homology concentration, hence boundedness. Extend both coefficient objects by zero using the preceding exact-flat-functor calculation. Applying this to an interval for W restricted to U gives finite_tor, and applying it to each supplied interval for L proves tor_bounds.

For each coefficient complex use finite induction on the finite interval of potentially nonzero homology degrees to refine all constructibility stratifications. Outside that interval use the zero-sheaf finite-local-constancy lemma. Intersect the two resulting stratifications with Stratification.inter. Concatenate this common stratification S with the trivial one-stratum stratification of the reduced closed complement using Stratification.openClosed. Define e and z by the two summands of finSumFinEquiv; its injectivity and surjectivity give range(e)={z}^c, including empty opens and empty complements. Exact-functor homology comparison and the open adjunction unit identify the restriction to each open stratum with the original homology sheaf. The disjoint-range vanishing theorem makes restriction to the complement zero. Transport finite local constancy along these isomorphisms.

tool_uses.why: Ordinary-etale bounded flat constructible models and their finite scalar extensions supply the precise Tor interval; the unit has no model-construction lemma.
Exact restriction of constant-module complexes is a generic site tool for checking the open input.
Generic ringed-topos pullback preserves K-flat flat-term resolutions and identifies restriction with coefficient tensor.
Generic bounded flat complexes give the Tor bound by definition; this does not replace a duality route.
Generic existence of flat-term K-flat representatives is needed to prove equality of actual chain maps.
Generic B-linear computation of derived scalar extension on K-flat representatives.
Ordinary-etale open projection comparison underlying the B-linear map.
The ordinary-etale sheaf counit has the section formula used in the explicit chain equality.
Exact ordinary-etale extension carries the displayed representatives and their cohomology.
Generic exact-functor cohomology identification gives H^q(j!K)=j!H^q(K).
Open-extension base change identifies the restrictions to each locally closed stratum and to the closed complement.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q34-a598d69ed (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the full maths of the five-step split of lem-coef-dualizing-open-tensor. The statement and stmt_deps are unchanged from side-live, which is still unsplit; there are no new nodes and no cycle, and every step is under 2000 characters. Step 1 applies lem-sp-etale-scalar-flat-model on the Noetherian Y with A→A (Stacks 03TT, read). The flat-term K-flat pullback (inverse-image-modules-exact (2), ringed-topoi pullback) and kun-flat-bounded-tor then show that L is ctf. Step 2 shows the chain map (j_!x)⊗b↦j_!(x⊗b) is the pur open-projection map (Stacks 0E8I, read). It is also the normalized q of lem-coef-etale-open-scalar-coherence (a uniqueness predicate on K-flat representatives), so d_L is B-linear and canonical. Step 3 is a genuine chain-level evaluation check using the explicit counit formula of extension-by-zero-adjunction (identity on V over U, 0 otherwise) and sheafification. Step 4 applies the flat model on U with A→B for the exact interval [a,b], j_! preserves flat sheaves, and the Tor bound follows over A and B with no flatness of B over A. Step 5 uses H^q(j_!K)=j_!H^q(K) and 03S6 base change to strata S⊂U (S×_YU=S) and to Z (empty), which gives the stratification clause. Edge cases U=∅, U=Y, m=n and non-flat Z/ℓ²→Z/ℓ all hold. There is no SGA or trf citation, and the 11 tool_uses are generic and accepted. Maintainer note: lem-sp-etale-open-counit-flat-models (Q05, created the same day) overlaps the item's flat-model and counit clauses in the étale case. It is normalized via β_j instead of d_L and lacks the stratification clause. Consider a merge or cross-citation. This is not a fault of this delivery.
